title: Reputation
summary: Reputation is a powerful force that precedes you and determines how people perceive you. It is built on surface-level actions, appearances, and words. A strong reputation can be established through honesty or good gestures to build trust, or by casting doubt on an opponent. However, going too far to defame an opponent can backfire and ruin your own reputation. If your reputation is damaged, it can be rebuilt by partnering with a highly respected person of opposite standing to project change.
example: P.T. Barnum used doubt and newspaper campaigns to destroy his opponent's reputation and build his own.
Thomas Edison ruined his own reputation by overstepping boundaries to defame Tesla, going as far as killing animals.
A legendary commander in the Chinese wars used his reputation to make enemies fear a trick and hesitate to attack.
reversal: There is no exception to this law, as you have nothing to gain from a damaged reputation and must master your reputation at all times.
